failure_summary.description: Selected a weaker consequence instead of the exact formula requested.
Misjudged which quantitative bound was established and confused parameter-dependent polynomial exponents with FPT running times.
Downgraded the claimed initial-time regularity without correctly assessing the stated compatibility conditions.
Accepted a one-way inclusion where the question asked for a complete classification.

patch.reasoning: The skill already addresses weaker consequences, exact classifications, and validating quantitative thresholds. The edits target two less explicit checks: distinguishing FPT from XP runtime forms, and assessing endpoint regularity against the compatibility conditions actually required.

edits.content:
## Parameterized running-time claims
- Normalize parameterized runtimes before classifying them: FPT has the form \(f(k)n^c\) with a constant exponent \(c\) independent of \(k\), while XP permits \(n^{g(k)}\). For example, \(2^{O(k\log n)}n^{O(1)}=n^{O(k)}\) is generally XP, not FPT; \(2^{O(k)}n^{O(1)}\) is FPT. Polynomial time for each fixed \(k\) alone does not establish a uniform FPT bound.
- For regularity claims, distinguish smoothness for positive time from smoothness up to the initial-time boundary. Check which compatibility conditions the stated result requires: do not invent extra ones, and do not infer endpoint smoothness from interior smoothing alone.
